purpose: Direct, accessible explanations of SCALE functionality and execution flow; technical evidence remains available behind the first answer.

coverage.semantic_claim: Bounded static and documentary topics; full functional, deployment and application acceptance remains open.

evidence_rules: SQL fingerprints bind original source definitions and exact redacted reading-copy bytes; spans are one-based reading-copy lines.
Article citations bind original retained source SHA and parsed node IDs.
Possible code behavior is not proof of active configuration, successful execution, a transaction's current state or process duration.
Attach current facts only from approved configuration-validation evidence, preserving scope, capture time and uncertainty.

accessibility.content_design: Short first answer, descriptive headings, ordered text steps, jargon defined where introduced; no chart/color dependency.
accessibility.future_insight_navigation: NOT_REGISTERED; do not invent screen paths or SOP actions.
accessibility.audience: Novice warehouse users, including users with visual impairments.

topics.title: Understanding shipment detail fields
topics.business_question: Why can a shipment summary field be blank?
topics.plain_answer: The summary combines the shipment header, containers, dock door and shipment lines. For some line-level fields, SCALE returns a blank summary when the lines contain different non-null values. A blank summary therefore does not always mean information is missing.
topics.trigger: An application detail-pane request bound to SHP_InsightDetailPaneData. The SDK documents the binding pattern; the active screen binding is not established.
input_context: Internal shipment number
Culture supplied by the screen

execution_steps.explanation: Read the shipment header view and call the status-name function for leading and trailing status.
Count containers whose tree-unit number equals their internal container number, filtered to the shipment.
Assign a dock-door number through the shipment-view/load join, then read LOCATION. This assignment has no shipment WHERE filter in the captured statement; it is a source-review concern.
For USER_DEF1..6, INVOICE and PICK_LIST_ID, return NULL when COUNT(DISTINCT field) exceeds one; otherwise return MIN(field).

configuration_dependencies: Screen binding determines whether this routine supplies the pane.
The SDK explains culture-based resources; passing culture does not establish that every deployed field is localized.
expected_results: Four SELECT result sets: header, parent-container count, dock-door information and detail-derived summary values.
The local dock-door variable assignment does not emit a fifth result set.
explanation_paths: A blank summary can result from differing line values, all-null values or no matching detail rows. These possibilities do not identify the cause for a specific shipment.
For an unexpected dock door, the unfiltered assignment is a source-review lead; no incorrect screen result was reproduced.
boundaries: No shipment records were read.
The SDK example and deployed signature differ; the deployed contract governs this database.
Current screen paths and bindings have not been registered.

cases.question: Why is the invoice blank in my summary?
must_explain: Explain the mixed-value rule and other null possibilities.
must_not_claim: A particular shipment has conflicting invoices.

cases.question: Does the routine return five result sets?
must_explain: It returns four; a variable-assignment SELECT is not a result set.
must_not_claim: Five SELECT statements necessarily produce five results.

topics.title: Understanding work monitor totals
topics.business_question: Why are work units, instructions and recently closed work different numbers?
topics.plain_answer: A work unit can contain several instructions. The group monitor counts distinct work units for chart groups, sums distinct-unit counts within conditions for its total, and counts instruction rows separately. Recently closed instructions come from active and inactive storage within a rolling one-hour timestamp window. Estimated time is stored planning data, not measured elapsed duration.
topics.trigger: An authorized application request to the named routines; active screen bindings/caller order are not established.
input_context: filterCriteria nvarchar(MAX), culture nvarchar(10); no defaults.
No parameters.

execution_steps.explanation: Parse warehouse filter and build the nonclosed detail-instruction chart.
Compute condition-grouped units, instructions and estimated time.
Count recently stamped closed details in active plus inactive storage, then return six summary values after the chart.

configuration_dependencies: Identify warehouse, grouping, condition, counting unit and rolling time window.
Check missing or duplicate filters before interpreting an empty result; no user-specific diagnostic was executed.
expected_results: Seven result sets. Empty data can yield NULL for some SUM totals, zero estimated time and zero recent-closed count.
explanation_paths: Identify the applicable branch, input/filter scope and configuration before attributing a result to a particular user.
Identify warehouse, grouping, condition, counting unit and rolling time window.
Check missing or duplicate filters before interpreting an empty result; no user-specific diagnostic was executed.
boundaries: A missing filter is not evidence of an empty warehouse.
The timestamp predicate does not establish exact completion-event time or throughput.
The SDK example and deployment have different result-set counts.
No operational rows or procedures were executed. Current configuration, runtime timing and screen navigation remain unverified.

cases.question: Why are empty totals partly blank?
must_explain: SUM can be NULL while COUNT and the ISNULL estimate are zero.
must_not_claim: No data always returns seven zero values.

cases.question: Did recently closed work disappear?
must_explain: The rolling timestamp window and storage filters matter.
must_not_claim: Work has been lost.

topics.title: Understanding which work is offered
topics.business_question: Why can two users receive different work?
topics.plain_answer: SCALE offers work using the supplied user, warehouse, work profile, locations, containers and feature settings. A work profile is a set of execution rules. Some branches prefer assigned work, apply location/priority order or limit the candidate list. Cart selection can also rewrite instruction sequence, so this procedure must not be run as a read-only diagnostic.
topics.trigger: An authorized application request to the named routines; active screen bindings/caller order are not established.
input_context: Thirteen declared inputs: workUnit nvarchar(50), containerId nvarchar(25), user nvarchar(30), workprofile nvarchar(25), workprofileSequence numeric(5), warehouse nvarchar(25), fromto int, fromLoc nvarchar(25), isSystemDirectedWork bit=0, isCartPickingWork bit=0, groupNumber int, transportContId nvarchar(25), isCcWorkUnit bit=0. Only the three bit flags have declared defaults.
feature nvarchar(100), user nvarchar(30); no defaults.

execution_steps.explanation: Cart regrouping can calculate and persist detail-instruction sequence before selecting candidates.
Read profile/sequence options, authorization and features, then build eligibility and ordering.
In eligible system-directed branches, probe priority and exact/greater/lower locations before executing the final parameter-bound candidate query.

configuration_dependencies: Some options are read by profile alone while others also use the supplied sequence; multiple sequence rows can therefore matter.
Missing or invalid top-row cap falls back to 2000 in the relevant performance branch; this does not identify its configured value.
An approved aggregate flag check cannot identify an individual operator's active profile.
expected_results: Branch-dependent work candidates and ordering; cart branch may first update stored sequence.
explanation_paths: Identify the applicable branch, input/filter scope and configuration before attributing a result to a particular user.
Some options are read by profile alone while others also use the supplied sequence; multiple sequence rows can therefore matter.
Missing or invalid top-row cap falls back to 2000 in the relevant performance branch; this does not identify its configured value.
An approved aggregate flag check cannot identify an individual operator's active profile.
boundaries: AIM describes profiles and ordered sequences generally. This procedure does not itself advance through all profile sequences.
Configured sort expressions and private business-code enumerations remain bounded review gaps; performance/legacy path equivalence is unproven.
No operational rows or procedures were executed. Current configuration, runtime timing and screen navigation remain unverified.

cases.question: Can support run work selection just to inspect configuration?
must_explain: It can mutate cart instruction sequence.
must_not_claim: The procedure is read-only.

cases.question: Does a missing cap mean unlimited work?
must_explain: The reviewed cap falls back to 2000 in the gated branch.
must_not_claim: Every query always returns 2000 rows.

cases.question: Does a profile select one deterministic detail row?
must_explain: Some reads lack sequence and ordering; distinguish their scope.
must_not_claim: Every profile-wide field came from the supplied sequence.

topics.title: Understanding an inventory adjustment
topics.business_question: Why can one inventory adjustment involve several operations?
topics.plain_answer: An adjustment can affect source quantities, destination quantities and serial numbers. The reviewed routine checks inputs and then calls the operations required by its quantity-effect flags. These flags specify which quantity categories should change. It is therefore more than editing one quantity field.
topics.trigger: A caller submits INV_AdjustInv with transaction and source/destination context.
input_context: Quantity, unit, item/company, transaction type and reference
Source/destination warehouse, location, container and inventory attributes
Effect flags for on-hand, allocated, in-transit and suspended quantities
Serial argument group, reversal and optional catch-weight context

execution_steps.explanation: If quantity is null/zero, both locations are null or item is null, create an audit message, call ADT_LogAudit and return before adjustment calls.
Convert dates, normalize zero attribute IDs and conditionally read serial-tracking/location-class rules; raise errors for coded disallowed combinations.
When the serial argument/effect conditions apply, validate and pick serial numbers, returning nonzero child codes immediately.
When source effect flags match, call INV_PickFromLocation and propagate SQL or nonzero child errors.
When destination flags match, call INV_PutIntoLocation with source attributes passed forward, then conditionally put serial numbers.

configuration_dependencies: ITEM serial tracking and LOCATION class affect conditional validation; those records were not read.
Caller-supplied effect flags and transaction type select branches; they are not universal warehouse settings.
expected_results: A sequence of validation and conditional child calls with early-exit paths.
Source and destination branches are conditional; every request does not necessarily run both.
explanation_paths: For a rejected adjustment, distinguish basic-input audit exit, serial/location validation and propagated child error.
For quantities changing differently, explain the effect categories and require actual transaction context before identifying an active effect.
boundaries: No adjustment or child procedure was executed.
This topic reviews the coordinator, not every child routine or caller-level rollback.
Complete transaction atomicity and a particular balance/serial condition are not established.

cases.question: Does an adjustment always move inventory between two locations?
must_explain: Source and destination calls are conditional.
must_not_claim: Every request calls both child routines.

cases.question: Does an error guarantee all earlier changes are rolled back?
must_explain: The coordinator propagates errors; caller transaction scope needs separate review.
must_not_claim: The visible sequence proves complete rollback.

topics.title: Understanding status changes at ship confirmation
topics.business_question: Why does ship confirmation affect lines, containers and the load?
topics.plain_answer: The reviewed status routine updates the shipment, its line quantities and its containers, then recalculates the load summary. The load's trailing status is the lowest trailing status among its shipments. A load can therefore still reflect another shipment that is less advanced.
topics.trigger: A caller invokes SHP_SetStatusesAtShipConfirm as one part of ship confirmation.
input_context: Internal shipment and load numbers
New status and status limit supplied by the caller

execution_steps.explanation: Read the shipment and active alert definitions; insert qualifying alert requests when the same alert/source/new-status request does not already exist.
Read the shipment warehouse, set header leading/trailing status and UTC ship time, and calculate warehouse-local status dates.
Shift and recombine detail status/quantity slots according to the supplied limit. The code excludes status1 = 995 from these updates.
Set the new status and timestamp on containers belonging to the shipment.
Set the load leading status and its trailing status to MIN(trailing_sts) across shipment headers on that load.

configuration_dependencies: Active WAREHOUSE_ALERT definitions and qualifying conditions control alert-request creation.
Warehouse timezone influences status dates.
New status and limit are inputs; the meaning of special status 995 is not established here.
expected_results: Related status changes across shipment header, detail, containers and load.
An alert request records work for later processing; it does not prove delivery of a notification.
explanation_paths: When load and shipment statuses differ, explain the aggregate rule before diagnosing an inconsistency.
When dates differ, distinguish UTC ship time from warehouse-local status dates.
boundaries: No ship confirmation was performed.
Carrier calls, labels, interfaces and caller-level commit/rollback are beyond this routine.
The duplicate existence check does not prove concurrency-safe exactly-once delivery.

cases.question: Why is my load's trailing status behind the shipment?
must_explain: Explain the minimum shipment trailing-status rule.
must_not_claim: A specific other shipment is causing it.

cases.question: Does an alert request prove the notification was sent?
must_explain: A request and downstream delivery are separate.
must_not_claim: External delivery succeeded.

topics.title: Understanding document choices and printer defaults
topics.business_question: Why do document choices and printer defaults depend on what I print?
topics.plain_answer: The routine reads the requesting user's default document and label printers. It then identifies the selected shipment, load or other item and returns the documents configured for that print process, including default choices. This prepares the selection screen; it does not confirm that printing finished.
topics.trigger: An application print-selection request calling MetaTrans_GetPrintSelectedDocuments.
input_context: Selected internal object number
Print-process code
Culture and username

execution_steps.explanation: Read the user's default document and label printers.
Select the entity by print process. Reviewed examples are load (30), cycle-count plan (20), shipment (70/170) and shipping container (80); other branches exist.
Return DOCUMENT_TYPE rows whose PRINT_PROC1..5 match, calculate default selection from DEFAULT1..5 and apply a feature-dependent exclusion.
Return entity/printer information and document choices for application binding.

configuration_dependencies: USER_PROFILE supplies personal printer defaults; usernames/printer names are not exposed by this topic.
DOCUMENT_TYPE defines process eligibility and default selections.
FEATURE_MANAGEMENT influences one exclusion; the feature literal is redacted.
expected_results: Selected entity context and eligible document choices with defaults.
A document can be eligible for multiple configured print processes.
explanation_paths: For a missing choice, distinguish document eligibility from default selection and later dispatch.
For different user defaults, explain the profile lookup without exposing another user's profile.
boundaries: No user profiles, printer names or transaction records were fetched.
No print job was sent.
The SDK example lacks the deployed username parameter; the deployed signature governs this database.

cases.question: Why is this document preselected?
must_explain: Matching document process/default fields determine selection.
must_not_claim: The current configuration has a particular value.

cases.question: The document is listed. Was it printed?
must_explain: Retrieval of choices and physical completion are separate.
must_not_claim: A physical print succeeded.

topics.title: Understanding an automatic receipt trailer link
topics.business_question: Why can a receipt gain a trailer link automatically?
topics.plain_answer: An enabled database trigger runs after receipt headers are inserted. A trigger is code the database runs automatically after a specified change. This trigger matches receipts to yard records by warehouse and trailer ID, requiring yard status 0, then writes the matching yard-record ID onto the receipt.

topics.title: How full, partial, short and overpick updates differ
topics.business_question: How full, partial, short and overpick updates differ?
topics.plain_answer: Full confirmation can move all of one side quantity even when the requested quantity is smaller. Partial confirmation subtracts only the request. Short and underpick rescale totals; overpick has a branch that rescales totals without replacing total quantity. Parent recalculation then sums all children and uses the summed from/to quantities for completion.
